decisions.reason: The same message already records the independently stated sanitation and hidden-liquid-trap requirements; the food-contact material rule requires no additional cleanability-state change.
Easy bowl removal was already required, and the existing same-message MODIFY fully captures the added cleaning, sanitation, and food-service contexts.
Quick whisk removal was already required, and the existing same-message MODIFY fully captures the added sanitation and food-service contexts.
The existing same-message MODIFY already generalizes isolation from the bottom-bowl seal to all liquids and removes the obsolete narrower attribute.
The food-contact material rule does not change the existing removable-spout behavior, and the reference to other removable components does not necessarily identify the spout.
The existing same-message MODIFY already captures the explicit requirement that parts remain accessible for maintenance, servicing, and replacement.
The same message already introduces the complete documentation-retention requirement; the food-contact material modification requires no further documentation-state change.
The spout is already specified as stainless steel, which is compatible with the approved food-contact material categories, so no spout-design attribute becomes stale.
The selected whisk is already stainless steel and remains compatible with the global food-contact material requirement without changing the whisk-head design state.
Approved food-contact materials do not alter the barista-facing or downward spout orientation.
The material decision does not change the required pour control, beverage preservation, dispensing path, or valve behavior.
The approved-material rule does not modify the existing requirement that plumbing and bowl seals prevent leakage into the base.
